title: Melbourne Wildflowers & Herbs
description: Native wildflowers, orchids, daisies and other herbs of Greater Melbourne.
attribution: Species lists and photos: iNaturalist contributors (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA). Text: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0).

cards.name: Nodding Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis nutans
cards.description: Pterostylis nutans, commonly known as the nodding greenhood or the parrot's beak orchid, is a species of orchid endemic to eastern Australia. Nodding greenhoods have flowers which "nod" or lean forwards strongly, have a deeply notched sinus and a curved, hairy labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis nutans has a rosette of between three and six egg-shaped to elliptic leaves, each leaf 15–30 mm (0.6–1 in) long and 10–20 mm (0.4–0.8 in) wide. The leaves are dark green, have a wavy edge and a distinct petiole.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Petra Holland, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Petra Holland

cards.name: Chocolate Lily
cards.subtitle: Arthropodium strictum
cards.description: Dichopogon strictus (syn. Arthropodium strictum), commonly known as chocolate lily, is a herbaceous perennial plant species native to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The species has up to 12 leaves that are linear or lanceolate in shape and are up to 65 cm long and 1–12 mm wide. The racemose inflorescence is up to 1 metre high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Thornhill, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Thornhill

cards.name: Waxlip Orchid
cards.subtitle: Glossodia major
cards.description: Glossodia major, commonly known as the waxlip orchid, parson-in-the-pulpit, or purple cockatoo is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae, and is endemic to Australia. It is a ground orchid with a single hairy leaf and one or two purple to mauve flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Glossodia major is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herbaceous plant with an underground tuber. It has a single dark green, hairy, oblong to lance-shaped leaf, 30–60 mm (1–2 in) long and 15–20 mm (0.6–0.8 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Milkmaids
cards.subtitle: Burchardia umbellata
cards.description: Burchardia umbellata, known as milkmaids, is a perennial herbaceous plant native to woodlands and heath of eastern and southern Australia. It is known in all states. It typically flowers from September until November, in dry sclerophyll forests.
cards.keyFeatures: The narrow leaves of Burchardia umbellata are up to 60 cm long by 1.5 to 4 mm wide. Clusters of white or pale pink flowers with reddish centers sit atop a thin stalk that is 50 to 60 cm high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rod Lowther, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rod Lowther

cards.name: Snowy Daisy-bush
cards.subtitle: Olearia lirata
cards.description: Olearia lirata, commonly known as snowy daisy-bush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a shrub with lance-shaped leaves and white and cream-coloured to yellow, daisy-like inflorescences.
cards.keyFeatures: Olearia lirata is a shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 4 m (13 ft) and has greyish branchlets. Its leaves are arranged alternately along the branchlets, lance-shaped, 30–150 mm (1.2–5.9 in) long, 5–25 mm (0.20–0.98 in) wide and petiolate, the edges of the leaves sometimes wavy or toothed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Small-leaved Clematis
cards.subtitle: Clematis microphylla
cards.description: Clematis microphylla (Small-leaved Clematis) is one of 8 Clematis species native to Australia. It occurs in all states and the ACT, but not in the Northern Territory. It is a common, quick-growing, small-leaved climbing species which prefers full sun and good drainage.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Rosy Hyacinth Orchid
cards.subtitle: Dipodium roseum
cards.description: Dipodium roseum, commonly known as rosy hyacinth-orchid or pink hyacinth-orchid, is a leafless saprophytic orchid found in east and south-eastern Australia. In summer it produces a tall flowering stem with up to fifty pale pink flowers with small, dark red spots. A widespread and common species it is often confused with D. punctatum but has darker, less heavily spotted flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Dipodium roseum is a leafless, tuberous, perennial, mycoheterotrophic herb. Between fifteen and fifty pale pink flowers with small dark red spots and 20–30 mm (0.8–1 in) wide are borne on a green to dark reddish black flowering stem 40–100 cm (20–40 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Kidney Weed
cards.subtitle: Dichondra repens
cards.description: Dichondra repens, commonly known as kidney weed, Mercury Bay weed, tom thumb, or yilibili in the Dharawal language, is a species of flowering plant in the family Convolvulaceae and is native to Australia, New Zealand, and the Indian Ocean islands, Mauritius, Réunion and Rodrigues. It is a perennial, herb with kidney-shaped to round leaves and small, greenish-yellow, star-shaped flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Dichondra repens is a perennial herb with a creeping habit, forming roots at the nodes. The leaves are kidney-shaped to circular, mostly 5–25 mm (0.20–0.98 in) long and 5–30 mm (0.20–1.18 in) wide on a petiole 10–50 mm (0.39–1.97 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: Bidgee-widgee
cards.subtitle: Acaena novae-zelandiae
cards.description: Acaena novae-zelandiae, commonly known as red bidibid, bidgee-widgee, buzzy and piri-piri bur, is a small herbaceous, prostrate perennial, native to New Zealand, Australia and New Guinea, of the family Rosaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Acaena novae-zelandiae is a small herbaceous perennial. It is stoloniferous with prostrate stems of 1.5 – 2 mm diameter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) James K. Douch, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Scented Sundew
cards.subtitle: Drosera aberrans
cards.description: Drosera aberrans is a perennial tuberous species in the genus Drosera that is native to New South Wales, South Australia, and Victoria. It grows in a rosette 3 to 5 cm in diameter with green, orange-yellow, or red leaves. It is native to southern inland South Australia, southern and central Victoria, and one single collection from New South Wales.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rolf Lawrenz, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rolf Lawrenz

cards.name: Tall Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis melagramma
cards.description: Pterostylis melagramma, commonly known as black-stripe leafy greenhood is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. Individual plants have either a rosette of three to six leaves or a flowering spike with up to twenty flowers and five to seven stem leaves. The flowers are translucent green with faint darker green lines and have a brownish-yellow labellum with a dark stripe.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis melagramma, is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber. Non-flowering plants have a rosette of between three and six narrow egg-shaped leaves, each leaf 13–50 mm (0.5–2 in) long and 4–11 mm (0.2–0.4 in) wide on a stalk 30–100 mm (1–4 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Richard Dimon, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Richard Dimon

cards.name: Pink Lady Fingers
cards.subtitle: Caladenia carnea
cards.description: Caladenia carnea, commonly known as pink fingers, is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to eastern and south-eastern Australia, including Tasmania. It has a single thin, green leaf and one to five white or pink flowers with red stripes and two rows of yellow-tipped "calli" on their labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia carnea is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single, sparsely hairy, narrow linear leaf, 90–150 mm (4–6 in) long and 3–4 mm (0.1–0.2 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Tall Sundew
cards.subtitle: Drosera auriculata
cards.description: Drosera peltata, commonly called the shield sundew or pale sundew, is a climbing or scrambling perennial tuberous species in the carnivorous plant genus Drosera. Among the tuberous sundews, D. peltata has the largest distribution, which includes eastern and western Australia, New Zealand, India, and most of Southeast Asia including the Philippines.
cards.keyFeatures: Drosera peltata is a perennial tuberous herb. Its underground tuber is generally found 4 – 6 cm under the soil surface, and its aerial parts range from 5 – 50 cm in height, with wide differentiation into several forms.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ian Rainbow

cards.name: Large Bird-orchid
cards.subtitle: Chiloglottis valida
cards.description: Chiloglottis valida, commonly known as large bird orchid or common bird orchid, is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia.It has two dark green leaves and a single greenish purple to purplish brown flower with six to ten blackish, column-like calli on the labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Chiloglottis valida is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with two dark green broad elliptic leaves 50–100 mm (2–4 in) long and 20–40 mm (0.8–2 in) wide. A single greenish purple to purplish brown flower 20–30 mm (0.8–1 in) long and 30–35 mm (1.2–1.4 in) wide is borne on a flowering stem 40–70 mm (2–3 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by yatesy

cards.name: Sifton Bush
cards.subtitle: Cassinia sifton
cards.description: Cassinia sifton, commonly known as sifton bush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia and an introduced species in other places. It is a multi-stemmed shrub with linear leaves, and more or less conical heads of 50 to 200 deep red to pale brown flowers. It is sometimes confused with Cassinia arcuata and authorities differ on its distribution.
cards.keyFeatures: Cassinia sifton is an erect, aromatic, multi-stemmed shrub that typically grows to a height of 1.2–2.0 m (3 ft 11 in – 6 ft 7 in), its branchlets with a few cottony hairs. The leaves are linear, mostly 6–9 mm (0.24–0.35 in) long and 0.5–0.7 mm (0.020–0.028 in) wide with the edges rolled under so that the leaves appear needle-shaped.
cards.imageCredit: (c) coenobita, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by coenobita

cards.name: Common Hovea
cards.subtitle: Hovea heterophylla
cards.description: Hovea linearis is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is an erect or trailing subshrub with mostly narrowly linear to linear leaves with stipules at the base, and mauve and yellowish-green, pea-like flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Hovea linearis is an erect or trailing subshrub that sometimes grows to a height of up to 1.2 m (3 ft 11 in), its branchlets covered with brown and silvery or grey hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) gmgoods, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by gmgoods

cards.name: Small Grass-tree
cards.subtitle: Xanthorrhoea minor
cards.description: Xanthorrhoea minor is a species of trunkless grasstree in the family Asphodelaceae native to south-eastern Australia. It was one of the many species authored by the Scottish botanist Robert Brown. Unlike some other species of grasstree, it lacks a trunk, and its leaves grow from one or more underground stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) guymer, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Common Rice-flower
cards.subtitle: Pimelea humilis
cards.description: Pimelea humilis, also known as common riceflower or dwarf riceflower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Thymelaeaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect or scrambling shrub with hairy stems, elliptic to lance-shaped leaves and heads of 12 to 52 of creamy-white, bisexual or female flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pimelea humilis is an erect or scrambling that typically grows to a height of 5–50 cm (2.0–19.7 in) and has densely hairy young stems. Its leaves are arranged in opposite pairs, narrowly elliptic to lance-shaped, mostly 5–16 mm (0.20–0.63 in) long, 1–9 mm (0.039–0.354 in) wide on a short petiole.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by yatesy

cards.name: Shiny Cassinia
cards.subtitle: Cassinia longifolia
cards.description: Cassinia longifolia, commonly known as shiny cassinia, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is an erect, aromatic shrub with sticky, hairy foliage, linear or oblong to narrow lance-shaped leaves, and heads of creamy-white flowers arranged in a dense corymb.
cards.keyFeatures: Cassinia longifolia is an erect, aromatic shrub that typically grows to a height of 1.2–2.5 m (3 ft 11 in – 8 ft 2 in), its foliage covered with short, glandular hairs and sticky. The leaves are linear or oblong to narrow lance-shaped, 15–95 mm (0.59–3.74 in) long and 2–6 mm (0.079–0.236 in) wide on a petiole 0.5–1 mm (0.020–0.039 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Cotton Fireweed
cards.subtitle: Senecio quadridentatus
cards.description: Senecio quadridentatus is native to Australia and New Zealand. In New Zealand it is known by its Māori name pahokoraka or pekapeka. Senecio quadridentatus is an annual or perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.
cards.keyFeatures: This erect plant, Senecio quadridentatus, is an annual or short-lived perennial herb up to around 1m tall. Generally speaking, it is a silver-looking plant from a distance which is attractive.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Christopher Stephens, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Christopher Stephens

cards.name: Early Nancy
cards.subtitle: Wurmbea dioica
cards.description: Wurmbea dioica, commonly known as early Nancy, is a species of plant in the family Colchicaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a herb with three linear to thread-like leaves and usually two to seven white flowers with a purple or greenish nectary band.
cards.keyFeatures: Wurmbea dioica is a herb that typically grows to a height of 3.5–40 cm (1.4–15.7 in) and has three linear to thread-like or tapering leaves 10–350 mm (0.39–13.78 in) long and 0.2–6 mm (0.0079–0.2362 in) wide with a sheathing base. Individual plants may have male-only, female-only or both male and female flowers and sometimes bisexual flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Wallflower Orchid
cards.subtitle: Diuris orientis
cards.description: Diuris orientis, commonly called the eastern donkey orchid or wallflower donkey orchid, is a species of orchid that is endemic to eastern Australia. Like others in the genus Diuris, it has two ear-like petals and is similar to the common donkey orchid (Diuris corymbosa) of Western Australia with which it has been confused.
cards.keyFeatures: Diuris orientis is a tuberous, perennial, terrestrial herb, usually growing to a height of 12–35 cm (5–10 in). There are up to three leaves arising from the base of the plant, each leaf linear to narrow lance-shaped, 10–30 cm (4–10 in) long, 5–10 mm (0.2–0.4 in) wide and channelled.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Leopard Orchid
cards.subtitle: Diuris pardina
cards.description: Diuris pardina, commonly known as the leopard orchid or leopard doubletail is a species of orchid which is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has two or three grass-like leaves and up to ten yellow flowers with reddish-brown marks and blotches.
cards.keyFeatures: Diuris pardina is a tuberous, perennial herb with two or three linear leaves 100–300 mm (4–10 in) long, 4–6 mm (0.2–0.2 in) wide and folded lengthwise. Between two and ten flowers 20–35 mm (0.8–1 in) wide are borne on a flowering stem 140–300 mm (6–10 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Slender Knotweed
cards.subtitle: Persicaria decipiens
cards.description: Persicaria decipiens, commonly known as slender knotweed, is a species of flowering plant native to Australia and Asia. Persicaria decipiens is a trailing plant whose stems grow horizontally at first but become more vertical with time, reaching 30 cm (1 ft) high. Its narrow elliptic to lanceolate (spear-shaped) leaves are 5–12 cm (2–4.5 in) long and 0.5–1.3 cm (0.20–0.51 in) across.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Terra Occ

cards.name: Maroonhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis pedunculata
cards.description: Pterostylis pedunculata, commonly known as the upright maroonhood or maroonhood, is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia. Flowering plants have a rosette of two to six stalked leaves and a single green flower which is white near its base and tinged with reddish brown to black and with a gap between the petals and lateral sepals. It is common and widespread in a range of habitats.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis pedunculata is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber. Flowering plants have a rosette of between two and six stalked leaves, each leaf 10–65 mm long and 5–20 mm wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Nina Kerr

cards.name: Small Poranthera
cards.subtitle: Poranthera microphylla
cards.description: Poranthera microphylla, commonly known as small poranthera, is a flowering plant in the family Phyllanthaceae. It is a small, widespread Australian herb with blue-grey leaves and white flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Poranthera microphylla is a decumbent or more or less upright, slender, densely branched, annual herb up to 30 cm (12 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Mountain Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis alpina
cards.description: Pterostylis alpina, commonly known as the mountain greenhood, is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has a rosette of fleshy leaves at the base and usually only one white flower with green markings and back-swept lateral sepals.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis alpina is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a rosette of three to five leaves surrounding the base of the flowering stem. Each leaf is egg-shaped to elliptic, 30–60 mm long and 15–30 mm wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eamonn Culhane, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Eamonn Culhane

cards.name: Twining Fringe-lily
cards.subtitle: Thysanotus patersonii
cards.description: Thysanotus patersonii, commonly known as twining fringe-lily or Paterson's fringed lily, is a species of flowering plant in the Asparagaceae family, and is endemic to Australia. It is a leafless, twining perennial herb, with tuberous roots, purple flowers borne singly or in sparse panicles with linear to lance-shaped sepals, elliptic, fringed petals and six stamens.
cards.keyFeatures: Thysanotus patersonii is a leafless, twining perennial herb with tuberous roots, the tubers about 2–5 cm (0.79–1.97 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rosalie Lawrence, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rosalie Lawrence

cards.name: Blueberry Lily
cards.subtitle: Dianella revoluta
cards.description: Dianella revoluta, commonly known as blueberry lily, blue flax-lily, or black-anther flax-lily, a species of flowering plant in the family Asphodelaceae and is endemic to, and widespread in Australia. It is a tufted, perennial herb with grass-like leaves and up to nine blue or violet flowers with six tepals, and stamens with bright yellow filaments and pale brown to almost black anthers.
cards.keyFeatures: Dianella revoluta is a tufted, perennial herb with stems less than 15 cm (5.9 in) long and touching or up to 30 cm (12 in) apart. The leaves are folded lengthwise and grass-like, 15–85 cm (5.9–33.5 in) long and 3–23 mm (0.12–0.91 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Blue Pincushion
cards.subtitle: Brunonia australis
cards.description: Brunonia australis, commonly known as the blue pincushion or native cornflower, is a perennial or annual herb that grows widely across Australia. It is found in woodlands, open forest and sand plains. In Cronquist's classification scheme it was the sole member of the monogeneric plant family Brunoniaceae.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Bulbine Lily
cards.subtitle: Bulbine bulbosa
cards.description: Bulbine bulbosa, commonly known as bulbine lily, native leek, golden lily, or native onion, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asphodelaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a perennial herb with thick roots, channelled leaves, and yellow flowers with hairy stamen filaments.
cards.keyFeatures: Bulbine bulbosa is a perennial herb that grows in tufts 27–75 cm (11–30 in) high with thick, fleshy roots and usually a bulb-like tuber. There are between three and seven leaves, channelled to more or less cylindrical, tapering and hollow, up to 30 cm (12 in) long and 1–5 mm (0.039–0.197 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Sticky Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Xerochrysum viscosum
cards.description: Xerochrysum viscosum (syn. Bracteantha viscosa (DC.) Anderb., Helichrysum viscosum Sieber ex Spreng., Helichrysum bracteatum var. viscosum Sieber ex DC., sticky everlasting) is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. The plant is native to Australia, occurring in Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania and the Australian Capital Territory
cards.keyFeatures: It is a sticky everlasting erect viscid herb. It is usually annual, though sometimes perennial, mainly flowers in spring and summer.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Matthew Lincoln, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Matthew Lincoln

cards.name: Tiger Orchid
cards.subtitle: Diuris sulphurea
cards.description: Diuris sulphurea, commonly called tiger orchid or hornet orchid, is a species of orchid which is endemic to eastern Australia. It has up to three leaves, and a flowering stem with up to seven bright yellow flowers with dark brown markings.
cards.keyFeatures: Diuris sulphurea is a tuberous, perennial herb with up to three linear to lance-shaped leaves 200–500 mm (8–20 in) long and 3–4 mm (0.1–0.2 in) wide. Up to seven flowers 20–30 mm (0.8–1 in) wide are borne on a flowering stem 200–500 mm (8–20 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kerri-Lee Harris, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kerri-Lee Harris

cards.name: Common Apple-berry
cards.subtitle: Billardiera mutabilis
cards.description: Billardiera mutabilis, commonly known as climbing apple berry, apple berry, snot berry, apple dumplings or changeable-flowered billardiera, is a species of flowering plant in the family Pittosporaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a slender climber or twiner with narrowly elliptic leaves and bell-shaped, greenish-yellow flowers that turn bluish as they age.
cards.keyFeatures: Billardiera mutabilis is a slender climber or twiner with silky-hairy new stems. Its adult leaves are mostly narrowly elliptic, 18–80 mm (0.71–3.15 in) long and 3–18 mm (0.12–0.71 in) wide on a petiole 2–4 mm (0.079–0.157 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Forest Hound’s-tongue
cards.subtitle: Hackelia latifolia
cards.description: Recorded 883 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) naturewatchwidow, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by naturewatchwidow

cards.name: Spotted Sun-orchid
cards.subtitle: Thelymitra ixioides
cards.description: Thelymitra ixioides, known as spotted sun orchid or dotted sun orchid, is a species of orchid that is native to southern and eastern Australia and to New Zealand. It has a single long, thin, dark green leaf and up to ten flowers which occur in a range of colours, most commonly blue to purple but usually with small, dark blue spots. It is a variable species, similar to T. juncifolia which has smaller flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Thelymitra ixioides is a tuberous, perennial herb with a single channelled or corrugated, dark green thread-like to lance-shaped leaf 200–300 mm (8–10 in) long and 10–15 mm (0.4–0.6 in) wide with a purplish base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Guy Taseski, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Guy Taseski

cards.name: Dolly Bush
cards.subtitle: Cassinia aculeata
cards.description: Cassinia aculeata, commonly known as common cassinia, dolly bush or dogwood, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect shrub with sessile, linear, variably-sized leaves, and heads of creamy-white to white flowers arranged in rounded cymes.
cards.keyFeatures: Cassinia aculeata is an erect shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–2.6 m (3 ft 3 in – 8 ft 6 in) and has densely hairy young stems, and flaky bark on the older branches. The leaves are sessile, linear, 3–50 mm (0.12–1.97 in) long and 0.7–2.0 mm (0.028–0.079 in) wide, often with the edges rolled under.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Creamy Candles
cards.subtitle: Stackhousia monogyna
cards.description: Stackhousia monogyna, commonly known as creamy stackhousia or creamy candles, is a flowering plant in the family Celastraceae. It is a small multi-stemmed plant with narrow leaves and terminal spikes of white, cream or yellow flowers. It is a widespread species found in all states of Australia but not the Northern Territory.
cards.keyFeatures: Stackhousia monogyna is a slender, multi-stemmed, perennial herb to 70 cm (28 in) high, covered with soft hairs or smooth on upright or ascending stems. The leaves are dark green, mostly narrow, linear to lance-shaped, up to 30 mm (1.2 in) long, 2–4 mm (0.079–0.157 in) wide and rounded, acute or with a short point at the apex.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lukas Clews, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lukas Clews

cards.name: Trim Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis concinna
cards.description: Pterostylis concinna, commonly known as the trim greenhood, is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia and which usually grows in colonies. It has a rosette of leaves at the base and a single dark green, white and orange-red flower.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis concinna has a rosette of between four and ten dark green, egg-shaped to oblong leaves, each leaf 6–30 mm (0.2–1 in) long and 5–15 mm (0.2–0.6 in) wide. A single dark green and white flower with an orange-red to brownish tip is borne on a flowering spike 80–300 mm (3–10 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cathy Powers, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cathy Powers

cards.name: Cut-leaved Daisy
cards.subtitle: Brachyscome multifida
cards.description: Brachyscome multifida commonly known as cut-leaved daisy, rocky daisy, and Hawkesbury daisy,is flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It has white, mauve or pink flowers and is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Brachyscome multifida is an ascending, smooth annual to 45 cm (18 in) high. The leaves are fine and deeply divided, 7 cm (2.8 in) long and 7-10 lobes 35 mm (1.4 in) long..
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Elspeth Swan

cards.name: Austral Stork's-bill
cards.subtitle: Pelargonium australe
cards.description: Pelargonium australe is a perennial herb that is endemic to Australia, and found in all states except the Northern Territory. Common names include native storksbill, wild geranium and austral storksbill.
cards.keyFeatures: The species grows to 50 cm high and has leaves with 5 to 7 lobes. Umbels of 4 to 12 flowers appear between October and March in the species' native range.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Vale Jenny Conolly

cards.name: Blue Stars
cards.subtitle: Chamaescilla corymbosa
cards.description: Chamaescilla corymbosa, commonly known as blue stars, blue squill or mudrurt, is a tuberous perennial herb species in the genus Chamaescilla. It is endemic to southern Australia. Plants are 10 to 15 cm high and have grass-like basal leaves The bright blue flowers have 6 petals (each with three nerves) and 6 stamens.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eamonn Culhane, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Eamonn Culhane

cards.name: Wiry Buttons
cards.subtitle: Leptorhynchos tenuifolius
cards.description: Leptorhynchos tenuifolius, commonly known as wiry buttons, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is an upright to ascending herb, multi-branched and has yellow flowers and grows in Victoria and South Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Leptorhynchos tenuifolius is a multi-stemmed upright to ascending multi-branched perennial, covered with soft hairs to smooth and 10–40 cm (3.9–15.7 in) high. Leaves are narrow, linear-shaped, pointed, margins recurved, 0.5–4 cm (0.20–1.57 in) long, 1 mm (0.039 in) wide, basal leaves longer and wider.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jared Shorma, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Common Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Chrysocephalum apiculatum
cards.description: Chrysocephalum apiculatum, known by the common names common everlasting and yellow buttons, is a perennial herb native to southern Australia. It is a member of the Asteraceae, the daisy family. The name "everlasting" was inspired by its use as a long-lasting cut flower.
cards.keyFeatures: The common everlasting grows to around 40 centimeters high, with spreading horizontal stems that turn upwards as they get longer. The elongated silvery grey leaves clasp tightly to the stems and are covered in fine, silky hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Small St John's Wort
cards.subtitle: Hypericum gramineum
cards.description: Hypericum gramineum, commonly known as small St. John's wort or grassy St. Johnswort, is species of flowering plant in the St.
cards.keyFeatures: Grassy St. Johnswort is a small annual or perennial herb with a height of 5–72 cm (2.0–28.3 in).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Ivy Leaved Violet
cards.subtitle: Viola hederacea
cards.description: Viola hederacea, the Australian violet, is a species of flowering plant in the family Violaceae, native to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The Latin specific epithet hederacea means "like ivy", referring to the leaves which resemble the leaves of Hedera species (which are not closely related). The flowers are usually rather pale and washed-out looking, the anterior petal (the one at the bottom of the flower when looking face on) is widest towards its apex, and the mature seeds are brown.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Drooping Mistletoe
cards.subtitle: Amyema pendula
cards.description: Amyema pendula, also known as drooping mistletoe or furry drooping mistletoe, is a species of flowering plant, an epiphytic hemiparasitic plant of the family Loranthaceae, found attached to several species of Australian eucalypt and occasionally on some species of Acacia. It is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is the most common mistletoe in Victoria, especially on the coastal side of the Great Dividing Range.
cards.imageCredit: (c) grampianshiker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Twiggy Daisy-Bush
cards.subtitle: Olearia ramulosa
cards.description: Olearia ramulosa, commonly known as twiggy daisy-bush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a shrub with narrowly elliptic, linear or narrowly egg-shaped leaves, and pale blue, mauve or white and yellow, daisy-like inflorescences.
cards.keyFeatures: Olearia ramulosa is a shrub that typically grows to a height of 1.6 m (5 ft 3 in). Its leaves are alternately arranged along the stems, narrowly elliptic, linear or narrowly egg-shaped with the narrower end towards tha base, 2–8 mm (0.079–0.315 in) long and 0.8–2.5 mm (0.031–0.098 in) wide with the edges rolled under.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Melburnian, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Small Shade Nettle
cards.subtitle: Australina pusilla
cards.description: Australina pusilla, the small shade nettle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Urticaceae, native to eastern Australia, and New Zealand. A highly variable perennial herb reaching 50 cm (20 in), it is often found growing alongside shady streams.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Jersey Cudweed
cards.subtitle: Pseudognaphalium luteoalbum
cards.description: Pseudognaphalium luteoalbum, synonyms including Helichrysum luteoalbum, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. In the United Kingdom, it is known as the Jersey cudweed.
cards.keyFeatures: It is an erect herbaceous biennial up to 70 cm (28 in) tall, branching from the base. Leaves are oblanceolate to lanceolate and covered in hairs like that of the edelweiss.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Millie Basden, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Millie Basden

cards.name: Fragrant Saltbush
cards.subtitle: Chenopodium parabolicum
cards.description: Chenopodium parabolicum (Syn. Rhagodia parabolica), commonly known as fragrant saltbush or mealy saltbush, is a shrub in the family Amaranthaceae. The species is native to Australia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Terra Occ

cards.name: Small Spider-orchid
cards.subtitle: Caladenia parva
cards.description: Caladenia parva is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a ground orchid with a single leaf and one or two green flowers with red stripes along the sepals and petals.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia parva is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single leaf, 30–100 mm (1–4 in) long, 5–10 mm (0.2–0.4 in) wide and which often has red spots near its base. One or two greenish flowers with red stripes are borne on a spike 50–150 mm (2–6 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lachlan Copeland, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Lachlan Copeland

cards.name: Hoary Sunray
cards.subtitle: Leucochrysum albicans
cards.description: Leucochrysum albicans, commonly known as hoary sunray, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is a small perennial with grey leaves, white or yellow flower-heads and is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Leucochrysum albicans is an upright, tufted perennial to 45 cm (18 in) high. The leaves are linear to oblong or broadly egg-shaped, woolly, 2–10 cm (0.79–3.94 in) long, 1–9 mm (0.039–0.354 in) wide, light grey and crowded near the base of the stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Nina Kerr

cards.name: Slender Speedwell
cards.subtitle: Veronica gracilis
cards.description: Recorded 626 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blushing Bindweed
cards.subtitle: Convolvulus angustissimus
cards.description: Convolvulus angustissimus commonly known as Australian bindweed, is a flowering plant in the family Convolvulaceae. It is a twining perennial with pink or white flowers and grows in Tasmania and mainland states of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Convolvulus angustissimus has slender, twisted, trailing branches with terete stems, hairy when young and grows to a height of 0.02 to 0.6 metres (0.07 to 1.97 ft). The leaf shape varies and grow along the length of the stems, basal leaves oblong to oval-shaped, margins toothed or slightly lobed and heart-shaped or squared.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Miguel de Salas, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Miguel de Salas

cards.name: Wine-lipped Spider-orchid
cards.subtitle: Caladenia oenochila
cards.description: Caladenia oenochila, commonly known as the red-lipped spider orchid, or wine-lipped spider orchid, is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to Victoria, Australia. It is a ground orchid with a single leaf and usually only one pale yellow-green flower with purple marks and a dark red labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia oenochila is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with a spherical underground tuber. It has a single, sparsely hairy, lance-shaped leaf, 70–120 mm (3–5 in) long and 8–12 mm (0.3–0.5 in) wide with reddish spots near the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Peter Crowcroft, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Native Flax
cards.subtitle: Linum marginale
cards.description: Linum marginale, commonly known as native flax or wild flax, is a species of flowering plant in the family Linaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a perennial herb with few branches, linear leaves, and blue flowers with five usually blue petals with darker veins.
cards.keyFeatures: Linum marginale is a glabrous, often glaucous, perennial herb that typically grows to a height of 10–60 cm (3.9–23.6 in) and has a single stem or a few, branching at the base. The leaves are linear to narrow elliptic, 5–20 mm (0.20–0.79 in) long and 1–3 mm (0.039–0.118 in) wide with a single vein.
cards.imageCredit: (c) gmgoods, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by gmgoods

cards.name: Parsnip Laceflower
cards.subtitle: Trachymene composita
cards.description: Recorded 585 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Brown Beaks
cards.subtitle: Lyperanthus suaveolens
cards.description: Lyperanthus suaveolens, commonly called brown beaks, is a species of orchid that is endemic to the eastern states of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Lyperanthus suaveolens is a tuberous, perennial herb, 18–44 cm (7–20 in) high with 2 to 8 yellowish brown, brown or dark reddish brown flowers, about 3 cm (1 in) wide, from August to November. The flowers are sometimes fragrant in warm weather.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lachlan Copeland, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Lachlan Copeland

cards.name: Elderberry Panax
cards.subtitle: Polyscias sambucifolia
cards.description: Polyscias sambucifolia, commonly known as elderberry panax or small basswood, is a species of plant native to eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Elderberry panax grows to 11 metres tall with a trunk diameter of 20 cm at Errinundra National Park and Otway National Park in the state of Victoria. The trunk is straight.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Leon Perrie, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Leon Perrie

cards.name: Eastern St Paul's-wort
cards.subtitle: Sigesbeckia orientalis
cards.description: Sigesbeckia orientalis, commonly known as Indian weed or common St. Paul's wort, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is a small, upright, sparsely branched shrub with yellow flowers and widespread in Asia, Africa and Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Sigesbeckia orientalis is an annual, upright herb or subshrub, about 0.4–1.5 m (1 ft 4 in – 4 ft 11 in) high, usually multi-branched with reddish coloured, hollow stems.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Forest Nightshade
cards.subtitle: Solanum prinophyllum
cards.description: Solanum prinophyllum, known as the forest nightshade or Grin Whiskers, is a accepted species of small plant native to the east coast of East Victoria to Southeast Queensland, Australia. S. prinophyllum is a short lived herb, annual or perennial.
cards.keyFeatures: Forest nightshade grows up to 50 cm high. Its leaves are 5 to 8 cm long and 3 to 5 cm wide.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Vale Jenny Conolly

cards.name: Small Mosquito-orchid
cards.subtitle: Acianthus pusillus
cards.description: Acianthus pusillus, commonly known as small mosquito orchid, is a species of flowering plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is a terrestrial herb with a single, heart-shaped leaf and up to 18 small, translucent green or pinkish flowers with reddish marking and a green to reddish-purple labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Acianthus pusillus is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, sympodial herb with a single heart-shaped, glabrous, dark green leaf which is reddish-purple on its lower surface. The leaf is 12–32 mm (0.5–1 in) long, 10–30 mm (0.4–1 in) wide on a stalk 30–80 mm (1–3 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Peter Crowcroft, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blunt Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis curta
cards.description: Pterostylis curta, commonly known as the blunt greenhood, is a species of orchid found in south-eastern Australia, Lord Howe Island and New Caledonia. It has a rosette of leaves at its base and a single white and green, forward leaning flower with a brown tip and a twisted labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis curta has a rosette of between two and six egg-shaped to elliptic leaves, each leaf 20–100 mm (0.8–4 in) long and 10–30 mm (0.4–1 in) wide. The leaves are dark green, have a distinct petiole and sometimes a wavy edge.
cards.imageCredit: (c) plantlookymagee, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Water Ribbons
cards.subtitle: Cycnogeton procerus
cards.description: Recorded 544 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by John Cull

cards.name: Rough Fireweed
cards.subtitle: Senecio hispidulus
cards.description: Senecio hispidulus, the hill fireweed or rough groundsel, is a species of flowering plant in the daisy family. It is found in many parts of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Senecio hispidulus is an erect herb with an annual or a short lived perennial life cycle and can grow up to 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) tall, but is usually between 30–100 cm (12–39 in) tall. It is a dicotyledonous herb which means the plant is vascular and that it flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blue Devil
cards.subtitle: Eryngium ovinum
cards.description: Eryngium ovinum, commonly known as the blue devil, is a plant species native to Australia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Matthew Lincoln, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Matthew Lincoln

cards.name: Common Raspwort
cards.subtitle: Gonocarpus tetragynus
cards.description: Gonocarpus tetragynus is an Australian herb in the watermilfoil family Haloragaceae native to eastern Australia. Common names include common raspwort. It is a widespread species particularly found in dry eucalyptus forests, scrubland, and heathland.
cards.keyFeatures: The herb can grow erect or ascend to 15-30 cm (5.9-11.8 in) tall. The many wiry branching stems can be smooth or are weakly 4-ribbed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Peter Crowcroft, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Crescent-cup Liverwort
cards.subtitle: Lunularia cruciata
cards.description: Lunularia is a genus of liverworts whose only species is Lunularia cruciata, the crescent-cup liverwort. Lunularia is either the only genus in the order Lunulariales, or may be placed in the order Marchantiales. The name, from Latin luna, moon, refers to the moon-shaped gemma cups.
cards.keyFeatures: Lunularia cruciata grows large, dichotomously branched green thalli with crescent shaped gemma cups containing disc-like gemmae. This is a unique morphological characteristic not possessed by other thalloid liverworts.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Mattia Menchetti, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Mattia Menchetti

cards.name: Small Tongue-orchid
cards.subtitle: Cryptostylis leptochila
cards.description: Cryptostylis leptochila, commonly known as small tongue orchid, is a species of orchid that is endemic to eastern Australia. It has one to a few broad leaves and up to fifteen green flowers with a dark red labellum that has a black stripe and rows of black dots either side of the stripe. As with others in the genus, it is pollinated by male ichneumon wasps.
cards.keyFeatures: Cryptostylis leptochila is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with one to several broad egg-shaped to broad lance-shaped leaves 18–120 mm (0.7–5 in) long and 25–40 mm (1–2 in) wide on a petiole 10–60 mm (0.4–2 in) long. The upper surface of the leaves is green but the lower side is reddish purple.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lek Khauv, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Mayfly Orchid
cards.subtitle: Acianthus caudatus
cards.description: Acianthus caudatus, commonly known as mayfly orchid, is a species of flowering plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is a terrestrial herb with a single egg-shaped or heart-shaped leaf and up to nine dark purplish flowers with thin, spreading sepals and petals, often with a musty odour.
cards.keyFeatures: Acianthus caudatus is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, sympodial herb with a single thin, egg-shaped to heart-shaped leaf which is dark green on the upper surface and reddish-purple on its lower surface. The leaf is 8–30 mm (0.3–1 in) long, 6–20 mm (0.2–0.8 in) wide and has wavy or minutely toothed edges.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Tasmanian Flax-lily
cards.subtitle: Dianella tasmanica
cards.description: Dianella tasmanica, commonly known as the Tasman flax-lily or Tasmanian flax-lily, is a herbaceous strappy perennial herb of the family Asphodelaceae, subfamily Hemerocallidoideae, found in southeastern Australia including Tasmania. Its leaves are up to 80 centimetres (30 inches) in length, and the flower stem is up to 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) tall. Blue flowers in spring and summer are followed by violet berries.
cards.keyFeatures: Dianella tasmanica is a strappy herbaceous plant which grows to 0.5–2 metres (1–7 ft) high and wide, with a thick spreading rhizome under the ground. The green linear keeled leaves have finely toothed margins, and may reach 1 m (40 in) in length and 1.5–4 cm wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Geoff Shuetrim, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Geoff Shuetrim

cards.name: Common Fringe-lily
cards.subtitle: Thysanotus tuberosus
cards.description: Thysanotus tuberosus, commonly known as fringed violet, fringed lily, or common fringe lily, is a species of flowering plant in the Asparagaceae family, and is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Thysanotus tuberosus is a tufted herb with a small rootstock, tuberous roots, cylindrical to elliptic tubers about 10–20 mm (0.39–0.79 in) long, 35–50 cm (14–20 in) from the rootstock. The 5 to 15 leaves are produced annually, linear, 200–600 mm (7.9–23.6 in) long, channelled below and more or less terete near the tip.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Australian Bluebell
cards.subtitle: Billardiera fusiformis
cards.description: Billardiera fusiformis, commonly known as Australian bluebell, is a species of flowering plant in the family Pittosporaceae and is endemic to the south-west of Western Australia. It is a sturdy, shrubby climber that has linear to narrowly elliptic leaves and blue, white or pink, nodding flowers arranged singly or in groups of up to four.
cards.keyFeatures: Billardiera fusiformis is a sturdy, shrubby climber, its new stems greenish and shaggy hairy, later reddish-brown. Its adult leaves are linear to narrowly elliptic, 25–50 mm (0.98–1.97 in) long, 2–6 mm (0.079–0.236 in) wide and sessile.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Salmon Sun-orchid
cards.subtitle: Thelymitra rubra
cards.description: Thelymitra rubra, commonly called salmon sun orchid or pink sun orchid, is a species of orchid endemic to southeastern Australia. It has a single thin, grass-like leaf and up to five salmon pink flowers with broad, toothed arms on the sides of the column. It is similar to T. carnea but the flowers are larger and the column arms are a different shape.
cards.keyFeatures: Thelymitra rubra is a tuberous, perennial herb with a single thin, channelled, green or purplish thread-like to linear leaf 80–200 mm (3–8 in) long and 3–5 mm (0.1–0.2 in) wide. There are up to five salmon pink flowers 20–25 mm (0.8–1 in) wide and are borne on a thin, wiry flowering stem 200–400 mm (8–20 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Common Cotula
cards.subtitle: Cotula australis
cards.description: Cotula australis is a species of plant in the daisy family known by the common names bachelor's buttons, annual buttonweed, southern waterbuttons and Australian waterbuttons. This small plant is native to Australia and New Zealand, but it is known in other areas of the world as a common weed (South America, California, Mexico, South Africa, etc.).
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Klaus Wehrlin

cards.name: Matted Flax-lily
cards.subtitle: Dianella amoena
cards.description: Dianella amoena, commonly known as the matted flax-lily, is an endangered, herbaceous, perennial plant endemic to Australia. It belongs to the family Asphodelaceae, subfamily Hemerocallidoideae. It has long grey-green leaves which grow in clumps from an underground rhizome, and displays blue-purple flowers in spring-summer, up to 90 cm in height.
cards.keyFeatures: The slender, grey-green leaves of Dianella amoena have a V-shaped cross section, and generally exhibit peg-like projections or “teeth” along the leaf midrib and margins. It is clonal, meaning one plant or colony consists of multiple genetically identical ramets connected via a rhizome, and it is capable of both vegetative (asexual), and sexual reproduction.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Englart, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Large Tongue Orchid
cards.subtitle: Cryptostylis subulata
cards.description: Cryptostylis subulata, commonly known as large tongue orchid, duckbill orchid or cow orchid, is a common and widespread orchid in south eastern Australia and New Zealand. It has relatively large, leathery, dark green to yellowish-green leaves and up to twenty yellowish flowers with a reddish-brown and dark purple labellum. It is often found in damp or swampy situations but also occurs in drier places.
cards.keyFeatures: Cryptostylis subulata is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with leathery, dark green to yellowish-green leaves which sit on petioles that are anywhere from 1 to 15 cm (0.5 to 6 in) long. The leaves are lance-shaped and measure 5–20 cm (2–8 in) long and 1–3 cm (0.5–1 in) across.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Vale Jenny Conolly

cards.name: Dwarf Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis nana
cards.description: Pterostylis nana, commonly known as the dwarf snail orchid, is a species of orchid endemic to Australia. It has a rosette of leaves at it base and a single narrow, bright green and white flower with a small labellum. There is uncertainty about its classification - some sources include South Australia and Western Australia in its range.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis nana is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a rosette of egg-shaped to heart-shaped leaves, each leaf 5–20 mm long and 3–10 mm wide. A single bright green and white flower, 10–15 mm long and 4–5 mm wide is borne on a stalk 50–150 mm high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Eastern Mantis Orchid
cards.subtitle: Caladenia tentaculata
cards.description: Caladenia tentaculata, commonly known as the eastern mantis orchid, large green-comb, green comb or fringed spider orchid is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a ground orchid with a single, hairy leaf and up to three green flowers with red stripes on the sepals and petals.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia tentaculata is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single hairy leaf, 80–150 mm long and 12–20 mm wide and often with red spots near the base. Up to three green flowers with red stripes and 60–100 mm across are borne on a spike 150–500 mm tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eamonn Culhane, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Eamonn Culhane

cards.name: Pale Flax-Lily
cards.subtitle: Dianella longifolia
cards.description: Dianella longifolia, commonly known as blueberry lily, pale flax lily or smooth flax lily, or blue flax-lily, (although other species, or the whole genus Dianella are also referred to by this last name) is a species of flowering plant in the family Asphodelaceae and is endemic to non-arid areas of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Dianella longifolia is a rhizomatous, perennial herb that forms tufts up to about 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) tall and has stems less than 10 cm (3.9 in) long. The leaves are folded lengthwise, grass-like, and 20–80 cm (7.9–31.5 in) long with a rounded to keeled sheath and 2–25 mm (0.079–0.984 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jean, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Musky Caps
cards.subtitle: Caladenia moschata
cards.description: Caladenia moschata, commonly known as musky caps or musky caladenia, is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to eastern and south-eastern Australia, including Tasmania. It is a ground orchid with a single leaf and up to five flowers which are dark-coloured on the back and white on the front, sometimes tinged with pink and with a strong musky or soapy odour.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia moschata is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and which grows singly or in small groups. It has a single, slightly hairy leaf 90–180 mm (4–7 in) long and 3–5 mm (0.1–0.2 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Black's Goodenia
cards.subtitle: Goodenia blackiana
cards.description: Goodenia blackiana, commonly known as Black's goodenia, is a species of flowering plant in the family Goodeniaceae and is endemic to southern Australia. It is a herb with egg-shaped to lance-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, and racemes of yellow flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Goodenia blackiana is a prostrate to ascending perennial herb that typically grows to a height of 200 mm (7.9 in), with stems up to 200 mm (7.9 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Murnong
cards.subtitle: Microseris walteri
cards.description: Microseris walteri is an Australian perennial herb with yellow flowers and edible tuberous roots, and one of three plants known as murnong or yam daisy along with Microseris scapigera and Microseris lanceolata. The plant is found in southern parts of Australia, including Victoria, NSW, ACT, SA, WA and Tasmania. In Victoria, the plant is widespread and occupies a wide range of habitats, particularly dry open forest.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Thornhill, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Thornhill

cards.name: Blue Finger-orchid
cards.subtitle: Cyanicula caerulea
cards.description: Cyanicula caerulea, commonly known as the eastern tiny blue china orchid, blue caladenia or blue fairy is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It has a single narrow leaf and a single blue flower.
cards.keyFeatures: Cyanicula caerulea is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single, sparsely hairy leaf, 20–70 mm (0.8–3 in) long, 2–5 mm (0.08–0.2 in) wide and which usually lies flat on the ground. A single pale to dark blue, rarely white flower 20–30 mm (0.8–1 in) long and wide is borne on a stalk 50–150 mm (2–6 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Purple Dewplant
cards.subtitle: Disphyma crassifolium
cards.description: Disphyma is a genus of flowering plants in the family Aizoaceae that are native to New Zealand, Australia, and the Cape Provinces of South Africa. Plants in this genus are prostrate, annual or short-lived perennial shrubs with succulent leaves and daisy-like flowers arranged singly on the ends of shoots with petal-like staminodes, many stamens and usually five styles.
cards.keyFeatures: Plants in the genus Disphyma are prostrate, annual plants or short-lived perennials with branches that root at nodes. The leaves are arranged alternately and fused at the base, succulent and round to more or less triangular in cross-section.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Purple Flag
cards.subtitle: Patersonia occidentalis
cards.description: Patersonia occidentalis, commonly known as purple flag, or long purple-flag, is a species of flowering plant in the family Iridaceae and is endemic to southern Australia. It is a tufted, rhizome-forming perennial with narrow, sharply-pointed, strap-like leaves, egg-shaped, bluish violet sepals and a cylindrical capsule. The Noongar name for the plant is komma.
cards.keyFeatures: Patersonia occidentalis is a tufted, rhizome-forming perennial that typically grows to a height of up to 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in). It has four to ten sharply-pointed, glabrous, strap-like leaves 80–550 mm (3.1–21.7 in) long and 2–10 mm (0.079–0.394 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lorraine Phelan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lorraine Phelan

cards.name: Australian Bugleweed
cards.subtitle: Lycopus australis
cards.description: Recorded 399 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Bower Spinach
cards.subtitle: Tetragonia implexicoma
cards.description: Tetragonia implexicoma, commonly known as bower spinach, is a species of plant in the Aizoaceae, or ice-plant family. A similar species is Tetragonia tetragonioides, however this species has larger leaves and a shorter flowering time.
cards.keyFeatures: Bower spinach is a scrambling subshrub that forms dense leafy patches of up to 4 metres (13 ft). The stems are long and trailing, often succulent and coloured red or pink when young, maturing to dark green to brown-black and becoming woody.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Guy Taseski, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Guy Taseski

cards.name: Blue Bottle-daisy
cards.subtitle: Lagenophora stipitata
cards.description: Lagenophora stipitata, commonly known as blue bottle-daisy or common lagenophora, is a small plant in the family Asteraceae, found in eastern mainland Australia and Tasmania, and also from South East China to East Asia, Java, and New Guinea. This species is a perennial herb that is stoloniferous and it has fibrous roots.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paul Whitington, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paul Whitington

cards.name: Angled Lobelia
cards.subtitle: Lobelia anceps
cards.description: Trimeris anceps (synonym Lobelia anceps), commonly known as angled lobelia, is a small herbaceous plant in the family Campanulaceae. It is a small, perennial herb with blue to purple flowers. It grows in several states of Australia, New Zealand, the Tubuai Islands, Chile, southern Africa, and Madagascar.
cards.keyFeatures: Lobelia anceps is a prostrate to ascending, glabrous, perennial herb typically growing to a height of 50 cm (20 in), occasionally branches rooting at nodes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Saryu Mae 前 朝琉, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Saryu Mae 前 朝琉

cards.name: Forest Pennywort
cards.subtitle: Hydrocotyle geraniifolia
cards.description: Hydrocotyle geraniifolia, commonly known as the forest pennywort, is a species of Hydrocotyle found in Australia. The habitat is moist forest floors often on the sides of hills.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Vale Jenny Conolly

cards.name: Purple Donkey Orchid
cards.subtitle: Diuris punctata
cards.description: Diuris punctata, commonly known as purple donkey orchid is a species of orchid which is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It has two grass-like leaves and up to ten purple or mauve flowers, often with darker, sometimes yellow marks. A yellow form from near Guyra is probably now extinct.
cards.keyFeatures: Diuris punctata is a tuberous, perennial herb with two linear leaves 150–300 mm (6–10 in) long, 3–4 mm (0.1–0.2 in) wide and folded lengthwise. Up to ten flowers 50–60 mm (2.0–2.4 in) wide are borne on a flowering stem 300–600 mm (10–20 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Coastal Burnweed
cards.subtitle: Senecio minimus
cards.description: Senecio minimus (syn. Erechtites minumus), commonly known as toothed fireweed and coastal burnweed, is a species of plant in the sunflower family. It is native to Australia (all 6 states) and New Zealand, and also naturalized on the Pacific Coast of the United States (Washington, Oregon, and California), as well as parts of Britain and Ireland.
cards.keyFeatures: Senecio minimus is an annual or perennial herb up to 200 cm (79 in) tall. Leaves are toothed but not pinnately lobed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lachlan Copeland, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Lachlan Copeland

cards.name: Australian Speedwell
cards.subtitle: Veronica plebeia
cards.description: Veronica plebeia, commonly known as creeping- or trailing speedwell, is a species of flowering plant belonging to the family Plantaginaceae. It is native to Australia and New Zealand. Robert Brown described the trailing speedwell in 1810 in his work Prodromus Florae Novae Hollandiae et Insulae Van Diemen.
cards.imageCredit: (c) guymer, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Purple Loosestrife
cards.subtitle: Lythrum salicaria
cards.description: Lythrum salicaria or purple loosestrife is a flowering plant belonging to the family Lythraceae. It should not be confused with other plants sharing the name loosestrife that are members of the genus Lysimachia in the family Primulaceae. This herbaceous perennial plant is native to temperate regions of Europe, Asia, northern Africa, and eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Lythrum salicaria can grow 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) tall, forming extensive clonal colonies, with numerous erect stems growing from a single woody root mass. The stems are reddish-purple and square in cross-section.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paul Roots, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paul Roots

cards.name: Climbing Sundew
cards.subtitle: Drosera planchonii
cards.description: Drosera planchonii or Climbing Sundew is a species of carnivorous plant endemic to Australia. It was first formally named in 1848.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lek Khauv, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Purple Beard Orchid
cards.subtitle: Calochilus robertsonii
cards.description: Calochilus robertsonii, commonly known as purple beard orchid or purplish beard orchid, is a species of orchid native to Australia and New Zealand. It has a single dark green leaf and up to nine green to brown flowers with reddish or purplish stripes. The labellum has a glossy purple, mauve, or bronze-coloured beard with a ridge between the "eye" spots.
cards.keyFeatures: Calochilus robertsonii is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single fleshy, dark green, linear to lance-shaped leaf which is 150–400 mm (6–20 in) long and 8–12 mm (0.3–0.5 in) wide. Unlike some others in the genus, the leaf is fully developed at flowering time.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Lady Fingers
cards.subtitle: Caladenia catenata
cards.description: Caladenia catenata, commonly known as white caladenia, white fingers and lady's fingers, is an Australian plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria. It is a ground orchid with a single hairy leaf and one or two white, sometimes pink flowers on a thin, sparsely-hairy stem.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia catenata is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single, sparsely hairy, linear leaf, 6–14 cm (2–6 in) long and 3–4 mm (0.1–0.2 in) wide. There are one or two flowers borne on a slender, sparsely hairy spike 10–30 cm (4–10 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Louise Docker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Grassland Sundew
cards.subtitle: Drosera hookeri
cards.description: Drosera hookeri, the grassland sundew is an shortly erect perennial tuberous species in the carnivorous plant genus Drosera. Drosera hookeri is found in south-eastern Australia. Although the holotype was collected in Tasmania, its distribution also includes Victoria, New South Wales and South Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Drosera hookeri is a perennial tuberous herb. Its underground tuber is white and generally found 2 – 5 cm under the soil surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Miguel de Salas, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Miguel de Salas

cards.name: Forest Starwort
cards.subtitle: Stellaria flaccida
cards.description: Stellaria flaccida, the forest starwort, is a wildflower found in eastern and southern Australia. A small ground covering plant. It may grow to 50 cm tall, but usually seen shorter than this.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Cobra Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis grandiflora
cards.description: Pterostylis grandiflora, commonly known as cobra greenhood or superb greenhood, is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia. As with similar orchids, the flowering plants differ from those which are not flowering. The non-flowering plants have a rosette of leaves but the flowering plants lack a rosette and have a single flower with leaves on the flowering spike.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis grandiflora is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and when not flowering, a rosette of four to nine egg-shaped leaves. Each leaf is 4–20 mm long and 3–10 mm wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Pigweed
cards.subtitle: Portulaca oleracea
cards.description: Portulaca oleracea (common purslane, also known as little hogweed, or pursley) is a succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae. All parts of the plant are edible raw or cooked.
cards.keyFeatures: Purslane grows from a taproot with fibrous secondary roots. The plant may reach 40 centimetres (16 inches) in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Forest and Kim Starr, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Eastern Bronzehood Orchid
cards.subtitle: Caladenia transitoria
cards.description: Caladenia transitoria, commonly known as green caps, is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has a single, long, erect, hairy leaf and one or two greenish-yellow flowers with purplish backs.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia transitoria is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and which usually grows in loose groups. It has a single erect, hairy, leaf, 60–100 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide which has a slightly reddish base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rod Lowther, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Slender Devil's Twine
cards.subtitle: Cassytha glabella
cards.description: Cassytha glabella, commonly known as the slender devil's twine, is a common twining plant of the Laurel family, found in many of the moister parts of Australia. A hemi-parasitic climber. The specific epithet glabella is from Latin, referring to the lack of hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paul Whitington, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paul Whitington

cards.name: Common Woodruff
cards.subtitle: Asperula conferta
cards.description: Asperula conferta is a species of flowering plant in the family Rubiaceae. It is Australian endemic distributed across Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania, South Australia and the Northern Territory.
cards.keyFeatures: Asperula conferta is a low spreading herb. It can grow up to 30 centimeters in height with leaves up to 16 mm in length.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kevin Sparrow, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kevin Sparrow

cards.name: Scrub Nettle
cards.subtitle: Urtica incisa
cards.description: Urtica incisa, commonly known as scrub nettle and stinging nettle, is a species of nettle native to Australia. It is also sparingly naturalised in New Zealand. A member of the Urticaceae, this species is typically found in disturbed areas in various habitats.
cards.keyFeatures: Urtica incisa (stinging nettle) is a mostly dioecious rhizomatous species of herb growing up to 2 metres (6 feet 7 inches) in height. The plant is usually unbranched.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Martin Hannan-Jones, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Martin Hannan-Jones

cards.name: Rainforest Crane's-bill
cards.subtitle: Geranium homeanum
cards.description: Recorded 311 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Hyssop Loosestrife
cards.subtitle: Lythrum hyssopifolia
cards.description: Lythrum hyssopifolia (orth. var. L. hyssopifolium) is a species of flowering plant in the loosestrife family known by the common names hyssop loosestrife and grass-poly. It is native to Europe but it is known elsewhere, including parts of Australia and eastern and western North America, as an introduced species and sometimes a weed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Emanuele Santarelli, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Emanuele Santarelli

cards.name: Dusky Fingers
cards.subtitle: Caladenia fuscata
cards.description: Caladenia fuscata, commonly known as dusky fingers, is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to eastern and south-eastern Australia, including Tasmania. It is a small ground orchid found in eucalyptus woodland and which flowers in September and October.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia fuscata is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single, sparsely hairy, narrow linear leaf, 5–18 cm (2–7 in) long and 2–3 mm (0.08–0.1 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Cushion Bush
cards.subtitle: Leucophyta brownii
cards.description: Leucophyta is a plant genus which is endemic to Australia. The genus was first formally described by botanist Robert Brown in 1818. The sole species in the genus is Leucophyta brownii, also known as cushion bush.
cards.imageCredit: (c) jirau, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Scaly-buttons
cards.subtitle: Leptorhynchos squamatus
cards.description: Leptorhynchos squamatus, commonly known as scaly buttons, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is an upright to ascending herb with variably shaped leaves and yellow flowers and grows in eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Leptorhynchos squamatus is an upright or ascending herb 10–40 cm (4–15.5 in) high, stems mostly simple, woolly to smooth and aging to reddish brown. Its leaves are oblong or narrowly oblong-lance shaped, 1.5–3.5 cm (0.59–1.38 in) long and 2–4 mm (0.079–0.157 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Sheep's Burr
cards.subtitle: Acaena echinata
cards.description: Acaena echinata, commonly known as sheep's burr, is a species of perennial herb, in the Rosaceae family, native to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: It grows to a height of 25–40 cm (9.84–15.75 in) and has shiny, green fern-like leaves 6–15 cm (2.36–5.91 in) long which are hairy on the underside. Its tiny pale green flowers form a spike and have purple stamens.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicole Kearney, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Nicole Kearney

cards.name: Red Beaks
cards.subtitle: Pyrorchis nigricans
cards.description: Pyrorchis nigricans, commonly known as red beaks, is a species of orchid endemic to Australia and is found in all Australian states except Queensland and the Northern Territory. It has a single large, oval leaf and up to eight relatively large red and white flowers. It usually only flowers after hot fires.
cards.keyFeatures: Pyrorchis nigricans is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single dark green leaf with red markings. The leaf is more or less oval in shape and 50–60 mm (2–2 in) in diameter and lies flat on the ground.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Veined Helmet-orchid
cards.subtitle: Corybas diemenicus
cards.description: Corybas diemenicus, commonly known as the stately helmet orchid or veined helmet orchid, is a species of terrestrial orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has round or heart-shaped leaf and a reddish purple flower with a central white patch.
cards.keyFeatures: Corybas diemenicus is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with a single round or heart-shaped leaf 15–25 mm (0.6–1 in) long and 12–20 mm (0.5–0.8 in) wide. The leaf is green on the upper surface and silvery green on the lower side.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Cowirrie

cards.name: Cinnamon Bells
cards.subtitle: Gastrodia sesamoides
cards.description: Gastrodia sesamoides, commonly known as cinnamon bells or common potato orchid in Australia and as the pot-bellied orchid or cinnamon sticks in New Zealand, is a leafless, terrestrial saprophytic orchid in the family Orchidaceae. It has a thin, fleshy brown flowering stem and up to twenty five drooping, brownish, self-pollinating flowers that are white inside.
cards.keyFeatures: Gastrodia sesamoides is a leafless, terrestrial saprophyte with an underground rhizome up to 80 mm (3 in) long and 30 mm (1 in) in diameter. The thin, fleshy brown flowering stem is 12–75 cm (5–30 in) tall with between three and six bracts 4–10 mm (0.2–0.4 in) long and between three and twenty five flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Parson's Bands
cards.subtitle: Eriochilus cucullatus
cards.description: Eriochilus cucullatus, commonly known as parson's bands, or leafless parson's bands, is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a common and widespread, slender ground orchid with a single leaf and up to five small white to pale pink flowers. It grows in all Australian states except Western Australia and the Northern Territory.
cards.keyFeatures: Eriochilus cucullatus is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber. It has a single, egg-shaped, dark green, slightly rough and hairy leaf which is not fully developed until after flowering, when it is 15–35 mm (0.6–1 in) long and 7–12 mm (0.3–0.5 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cathy Powers, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cathy Powers

cards.name: Berry Saltbush
cards.subtitle: Atriplex semibaccata
cards.description: Atriplex semibaccata, commonly known as Australian saltbush, berry saltbush, or creeping saltbush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a perennial herb native to Western Australia, South Australia, Queensland and New South Wales, but has been introduced into other states and to overseas countries.
cards.keyFeatures: Atriplex semibaccata is a taproot perennial herb, that has prostrated and decumbent characteristics. Native to Australia and widespread in all mainland Australian states, A. semibaccata thrives in harsh and saline conditions.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Swamp Pennywort
cards.subtitle: Centella cordifolia
cards.description: Centella cordifolia, commonly known as swamp pennywort or arthritis herb, is a trailing perennial herb native to Australia. The species is common in preferred local environments. It potentially has medicinal purposes and indigenous cultural significance.
cards.keyFeatures: Centella cordifolia is a groundcover herb that can grow up to 15 cm (5.9 in) tall, and typically stretches 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) wide. Leaves are heart-shaped (cordate), glabrescent, glossy and dark green.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Variable Plantain
cards.subtitle: Plantago varia
cards.description: Recorded 263 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by yatesy

cards.name: Slender Bottle-daisy
cards.subtitle: Lagenophora sublyrata
cards.description: Recorded 263 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Lesser Joyweed
cards.subtitle: Alternanthera denticulata
cards.description: Alternanthera denticulata (common name lesser joyweed) is a small prostrate white-flowering herb in the Amaranthaceae family. It is native to all states and territories of Australia, New Guinea, and the North Island of New Zealand. It is also one of the food plants of the varied eggfly, Hypolimnas bolina nerina.
cards.keyFeatures: Alternanthera denticulata is a prostrate to erect perennial herb, whose stems root at the nodes. The stems are green flushed pink, and sparsely hairy to being without a covering.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Variable Stinkweed
cards.subtitle: Opercularia varia
cards.description: Recorded 257 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by corunastylis

cards.name: Australian Buttercup
cards.subtitle: Ranunculus lappaceus
cards.description: Ranunculus lappaceus, commonly known as the common buttercup, Australian buttercup or Yarrakalgamba, is found across eastern Australia. Like buttercups elsewhere, it is a perennial herb with yellow flowers appearing in spring and summer. James Edward Smith described it in 1815, and it still bears its original name.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Tufted Blue Lily
cards.subtitle: Thelionema caespitosum
cards.description: Thelionema caespitosum, the tufted lily or tufted blue-lily, is a species of perennial herb, native to Australia. The lily-like flowers are blue, light blue, pale yellow or white and have yellow stamens. The species occurs in the Northern Territory, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Spiny Rice-Flower
cards.subtitle: Pimelea spinescens
cards.description: Pimelea spinescens, commonly known as plains rice-flower, spiny rice-flower or prickly pimelea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Thymelaeaceae and is endemic to Victoria. It is a spreading undershrub with elliptic leaves arranged in opposite pairs, and heads of white, cream-coloured or yellow flowers surrounded by 4 elliptic, leaf-like involucral bracts.
cards.keyFeatures: Pimelea spinescens is a spreading, stunted, long-lived undershrub that typically grows to a height of 5–30 cm (2.0–11.8 in). It has a deep taproot and its stems are glabrous, becoming spiny as they mature.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Mountain Helmet-orchid
cards.subtitle: Corybas grumulus
cards.description: Recorded 246 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)
