cards.keyFeatures: Centipeda cunninghamii is an erect or ascending, endemic Australian perennial herb of the Daisy family (Asteraceae), glabrous or rarely woolly, about 20 cm (8 inches) high; stems much-branched. Leaves: Oblong to more less spathulate, they are about 15 mm wide; margins shallowly toothed or subentire; narrowed to base but petiole indistinct.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Three-veined Cassinia
cards.subtitle: Cassinia trinerva
cards.description: Cassinia trinerva is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect shrub or small tree with hairy stems, narrow lance-shaped leaves, and flower heads arranged in dense corymbs.
cards.keyFeatures: Cassinia trinerva is an erect shrub or tree that typically grows to a height of up to about 8 m (26 ft), its branchlets sticky and covered with glandular and cottony hairs. The leaves are narrow lance-shaped, 30–120 mm (1.2–4.7 in) long and 3.5–6 mm (0.14–0.24 in) wide on a petiole 1–4 mm (0.039–0.157 in) long with three longitudinal veins.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Max Campbell, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Max Campbell

cards.name: Slender Tick-trefoil
cards.subtitle: Desmodium varians
cards.description: Desmodium varians is a small climbing or prostrate herb in the family Fabaceae. A widespread species but not commonly seen, found in eastern Australia. Attractive pink flowers may form at any time of the year.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Green Mulla Mulla
cards.subtitle: Ptilotus macrocephalus
cards.description: Ptilotus macrocephalus, commonly known as green pussytails or featherheads, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a glabrous or slightly hairy perennial herb, with a woody taproot, linear to narrowly lance-shaped leaves and dense oblong to cylindrical spikes of yellowish green or silvery white flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Ptilotus macrocephalus is a glabrous or slightly hairy perennial herb with a woody taproot, that typically grows to a height of up to about 50 cm (20 in). Its leaves are linear to narrowly lance-shaped or narrowly egg-shaped, about 30–100 mm (1.2–3.9 in) long and 4–12 mm (0.16–0.47 in) wide and thickish and crowded near the base or forming a rosette.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Twisted Sun-orchid
cards.subtitle: Thelymitra flexuosa
cards.description: Thelymitra flexuosa, known as twisted sun orchid, is a species of orchid that is endemic to southern Australia. It has a single thin, wiry leaf and up to four cream-coloured to canary yellow flowers with four rows of short hairs on the back of the column. It is a common and widespread species, superficially similar to T. antennifera.
cards.keyFeatures: Thelymitra flexuosa is a tuberous, perennial herb with a single wiry, linear leaf 60–150 mm (2–6 in) long and 3–4 mm (0.1–0.2 in) wide. Up to four cream-coloured to canary yellow 10–15 mm (0.4–0.6 in) wide borne on a flowering stem 200–350 mm (8–10 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cal Wood, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cal Wood

cards.name: Pink Bladderwort
cards.subtitle: Utricularia tenella
cards.description: Utricularia tenella is a terrestrial carnivorous plant that belongs to the genus Utricularia (family Lentibulariaceae). Its distribution includes areas in Western Australia, South Australia, Victoria, and Tasmania.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Hugo Innes, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Hugo Innes

cards.name: Three-ribbed Arrowgrass
cards.subtitle: Triglochin striata
cards.description: Triglochin striata is a species of flowering plant in the family Juncaginaceae. It is native to New Zealand, South America, America, Africa, Australia and Southern Portugal. It is a perennial with parallel lines on its narrow linear leaves, which gives rise to its common name streaked arrow grass.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Joe Potter Butler, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Spoon Leaved Cudweed
cards.subtitle: Stuartina muelleri
cards.description: Recorded 59 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Pale Swamp Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Coronidium gunnianum
cards.description: Coronidium gunnianum, commonly known as pale swamp everlasting, pale everlasting or Gunn's everlasting is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect perennial, with linear to lance-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, and solitary heads of pale yellow to brownish yellow daisy-like flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Coronidium gunnianum is an erect, rhizomatous perennial that typically grows to a height of 50 cm (20 in) with few branches, and stems covered in cottony hairs pressed against the surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Round-leaf Wilsonia
cards.subtitle: Wilsonia rotundifolia
cards.description: Recorded 58 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Fluffy Groundsel
cards.subtitle: Senecio macrocarpus
cards.description: Recorded 58 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Nina Kerr

cards.name: Fishweed
cards.subtitle: Chenopodium trigonon
cards.description: Recorded 57 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Elbow Orchid
cards.subtitle: Thynninorchis huntiana
cards.description: Arthrochilus huntianus, commonly known as common elbow orchid, is a flowering plant in the orchid family (Orchidaceae) and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has no leaves but an insect-like flower which has its labellum dangling like a lure away from the rest of the flower. Because of its thin, wiry stem and small, dull-coloured flowers, this orchid is difficult to locate.
cards.keyFeatures: Arthrochilus huntianus is a leafless terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, sympodial herb with an underground tuber which produces daughter tubers on the end of root-like stolons. Up to ten insect-like flowers 9–11 mm (0.35–0.43 in) long and about 1.5 mm (0.06 in) wide are borne on a thin, wiry, green to reddish flowering stem 60–150 mm (2–6 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Tiny Bladderwort
cards.subtitle: Utricularia lateriflora
cards.description: Utricularia lateriflora, the small bladderwort, is a small to medium-sized perennial carnivorous plant that belongs to the genus Utricularia. U. lateriflora is endemic to Australia and can be found in New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, and Victoria. It grows as a terrestrial plant in sandy or peaty soils in heathland at lower altitudes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Noah Elhardt, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Short Purple-flag
cards.subtitle: Patersonia fragilis
cards.description: Patersonia fragilis, commonly known as swamp iris or short purple-flag, is a species of flowering plant in the family Iridaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is a tufted perennial herb with linear, cylindrical leaves and pale violet to blue-violet flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Patersonia fragilis is a tufted or clump-forming perennial herb that typically grows to a height of 30–50 cm (12–20 in). There are three to six narrowly linear leaves 220–550 mm (8.7–21.7 in) long and 1–3 mm (0.039–0.118 in) wide on each shoot.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Bearded Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis plumosa
cards.description: Pterostylis plumosa, commonly known as the bearded greenhood or plumed greenhood is a species of orchid in the family Orchidaceae which is endemic to south-eastern Australia and possibly New Zealand. Its labellum or lip is long and thin, bordered with golden hairs, giving it the name "bearded".
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis plumosa is a perennial herb rising from round tubers to form small colonies and grows to a height of 12–20 centimetres (5–8 in). It has 5-20 fleshy lance-shaped, pale green leaves crowded around the base of the stem and extending upwards, 10–30 millimetres (0.4–1 in) long and 5–15 millimetres (0.2–0.6 in)wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rolf Lawrenz, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rolf Lawrenz

cards.name: Digger's Speedwell
cards.subtitle: Veronica perfoliata
cards.description: Veronica perfoliata, commonly known as digger's speedwell, is a common perennial herb found at higher altitudes in south-eastern Australia. It is a low-growing multi-stemmed plant rising from a woody rootstock. It has rounded blue-grey foliage and sprays of intense violet-blue flowers at the end of arching branches.
cards.keyFeatures: Veronica perfoliata is an erect woody herb with arching decumbent branches 120 cm (47 in) long. The leaves are smooth and bluish green with a powdery bloom, about 1.5–5.5 cm (0.59–2.2 in) long and 15–40 mm (0.59–1.6 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Bristly Waterpepper
cards.subtitle: Persicaria subsessilis
cards.description: Recorded 55 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Hairy Stylewort
cards.subtitle: Levenhookia dubia
cards.description: Levenhookia dubia, the hairy stylewort, is a dicotyledonous plant that belongs to the genus Levenhookia (family Stylidiaceae). It is an ephemeral annual that grows from 2–6 centimetres (0.79–2.36 in) tall with obovate leaves that are generally 2–5 millimetres (0.079–0.197 in) long. Flowers are white and bloom from September to October in its native range.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kevin Thiele, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Wireleaf Mistletoe
cards.subtitle: Amyema preissii
cards.description: Amyema preissii, commonly known as wireleaf mistletoe, is a species of mistletoe, an epiphytic, hemiparasitic plant of the family Loranthaceae. It is native to Australia where it has been recorded from all mainland states. The flowers are red and up to 26 mm long.
cards.keyFeatures: Amyema Preissii is the only mistletoe with slender, needle-shaped leaves and all-red flowers lacking velvety covering, in groups of three. This distinctive mistletoe has feathery foliage, composed of soft, needle-like leaves (with pointed, but not sharp, tips).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rosalie Lawrence, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rosalie Lawrence

cards.name: Basalt Podolepis
cards.subtitle: Podolepis linearifolia
cards.description: Recorded 54 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Creeping Knotweed
cards.subtitle: Persicaria prostrata
cards.description: Persicaria prostrata, basionym Polygonum prostratum, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to Australia and perhaps New Zealand. It is known by the common name of creeping knotweed.
cards.keyFeatures: Decumbent perennial herb with stems up to about 40 cm long. Leaves lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, 1–5 cm long, 3–10 mm wide with short hairs on the margins and main veins.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Pink Sun-orchid
cards.subtitle: Thelymitra carnea
cards.description: Thelymitra carnea, commonly called tiny sun orchid or pinkish sun orchid, is a species of orchid that is native to Australia and New Zealand. It has narrow, almost cylindrical leaves and up to four relatively small pale to deep pink flowers on a wiry, zig-zag stem.
cards.keyFeatures: Thelymitra carnea is a tuberous, perennial herb with a single channelled, linear, almost cylinder-shaped leaf 60–150 mm (2–6 in) long and 1–1.5 mm (0.04–0.06 in) wide. Up to four pale to deep pink flowers 8–15 mm (0.3–0.6 in) wide are borne on a wiry, zig-zag flowering stem 200–350 mm (8–10 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bill Campbell, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Bill Campbell

cards.name: Native Violet
cards.subtitle: Viola betonicifolia
cards.description: Viola betonicifolia, commonly known as the arrowhead violet, showy violet or mountain violet, is a small perennial of the genus Viola, which contains pansies and violets. It occurs from India and Pakistan in southern Asia throughout eastern Australia and Tasmania. It grows in shaded habitat in forests.
cards.keyFeatures: This species is distinguished by long, slender arrow-shaped leaves that grow from the base of the plant, which has no stem as such, and are up to 6 cm (2.5 in) long with a v-shaped sinus at the base, and are usually rather bright, fresh green. Its striking bright purple flowers are 1–1.5 cm (0.4–0.6 in) in diameter and occur in spring and summer.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Small Helmet-orchid
cards.subtitle: Corybas unguiculatus
cards.description: Corybas unguiculatus, commonly known as the small helmet orchid or pelicans, is a species of terrestrial orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a widespread, sometimes common but small orchid with a single leaf and a single reddish purple to reddish black flower.
cards.keyFeatures: Corybas unguiculatus is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with a single egg-shaped, heart-shaped or round leaf 5–30 mm (0.2–1 in) long and 10–20 mm (0.4–0.8 in) wide. The leaf is greyish green on the upper surface and reddish on the lower side.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lachlan Copeland, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Lachlan Copeland

cards.name: Waterpepper
cards.subtitle: Persicaria hydropiper
cards.description: Persicaria hydropiper (syn. Polygonum hydropiper), also known as water pepper, marshpepper knotweed, arse smart or tade, is a plant of the family Polygonaceae. A widespread species, Persicaria hydropiper is found in Australia, New Zealand, temperate Asia, Europe and North America.
cards.keyFeatures: Water pepper is an annual herb with an erect stem growing to a height of 20 to 70 cm (8 to 28 in). The leaves are alternate and almost stalkless.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Татьяна Горбушина

cards.name: Australian Stonecrop
cards.subtitle: Crassula sieberiana
cards.description: Crassula sieberiana, the Australian stonecrop, is a succulent plant found in a variety of habitats in Australia, New Zealand and Lord Howe Island. It has been introduced to Hawaii. Usually seen in rock crevices.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Guy Taseski, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Guy Taseski

cards.name: Rosy Sundew
cards.subtitle: Drosera spatulata
cards.description: Drosera spatulata, the spoon-leaved sundew, is a variable, rosette-forming sundew with spoon-shaped leaves. The specific epithet is Latin for "spatula shaped," a reference to the form of the leaves. This sundew has a large range and occurs naturally throughout Southeast Asia, southern China and Japan, Micronesia, Papua New Guinea, eastern Australia, Tasmania and New Zealand.
cards.keyFeatures: Drosera spatulata is a variable perennial plant that produces small rosettes of numerous spathulate leaves. This species is widely variable, but generally plants are about 4 cm (1.6 in) in diameter.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Swamp Mallet
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus spathulata
cards.description: Eucalyptus spathulata, commonly known as swamp mallet, narrow leaved gimlet or swamp gimlet, is a species of mallet that is endemic to Western Australia. It has a dense crown, smooth, satin-like bark, glossy green, linear leaves, flower buds in groups of three or seven, white flowers and cup-shaped to conical fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus spathulata is a low-branching mallet with a dense crown that typically grows to a height of 8–12 m (26–39 ft) but does not form a lignotuber. The trunk usually has a diameter of 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) but can be even larger for older trees, and it is usually relatively short, sometimes fluted at the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Donald Davesne, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: River Buttercup
cards.subtitle: Ranunculus inundatus
cards.description: Ranunculus inundatus, commonly known as the river buttercup, is a species of buttercup found in eastern Australia. The plant has found some recent relevance within the freshwater aquascaping and home aquarium/vivarium hobbies, particularly amongst enthusiasts of nano aquariums.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Richard Fuller

cards.name: Tiny Star
cards.subtitle: Pauridia glabella
cards.description: Recorded 49 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Brittle Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis truncata
cards.description: Pterostylis truncata, commonly known as the brittle greenhood or little dumpies, is a species of orchid endemic to eastern Australia. It is easily distinguished from other greenhood orchids by its short habit and relatively large, "dumpy", green, white and brown flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: When not flowering, Pterostylis truncata has a rosette of between two and six bright green, egg-shaped to lance-shaped leaves, each leaf 10–35 mm (0.4–1 in) long and 5–18 mm (0.2–0.7 in) wide. When it flowers it produces a single white flower with green and brown stripes, borne on a spike 50–150 mm (2–6 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Green Bird Orchid
cards.subtitle: Chiloglottis cornuta
cards.description: Chiloglottis cornuta, commonly known as the green bird orchid, is a species of orchid found in south-eastern Australia and in New Zealand, including many of its offshore islands. It has two broad leaves and a single green or pinkish flower with six to eight rounded, flattened green, reddish or blackish calli on the labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Chiloglottis cornuta is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with two elliptic leaves 60–100 mm (2–4 in) long and 20–30 mm (0.8–1 in) wide on a petiole 5–10 mm (0.2–0.4 in) long. A single green to reddish flower 13–16 mm (0.5–0.6 in) long and 25–30 mm (0.98–1.2 in) wide is borne on a flowering stem 40–100 mm (2–4 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Taylor Davies-Colley, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Taylor Davies-Colley

cards.name: Slender Palm Lily
cards.subtitle: Cordyline stricta
cards.description: Cordyline stricta, known as the slender palm lily or narrow-leaved palm lily, is an evergreen Australian plant. A shrub to 5 metres tall found in wet sclerophyll forest and rainforest, usually on the coastal lowlands. From near Bilpin, New South Wales further north to Queensland.
cards.keyFeatures: Leaves are long and thin, 30 to 50 cm long, 1 to 2 cm wide. Mauve flowers form on panicles, 20 to 40 cm long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Steve Llewellyn, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Derwent Speedwell
cards.subtitle: Veronica derwentiana
cards.description: Veronica derwentiana, commonly known as Derwent speedwell, is a flowering plant species of the family Plantaginaceae, endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a perennial with toothed leaves and white or pale blue flowers in terminal sprays in spring and summer.
cards.keyFeatures: Veronica derwentiana is a woody herb which grows to 140 cm (55 in) high with numerous upright stems from a woody rootstock. The stems are smooth or have small hairs lying longitudinal, occasionally on the whole surface and not branched below the flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Mainland Striped Greenhood
cards.subtitle: Pterostylis striata
cards.description: Pterostylis striata, commonly known as the mainland striped greenhood, is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern mainland Australia. As with similar orchids, the flowering plants differ from those which are not flowering. The non-flowering plants have a rosette of leaves but the flowering plants have a single flower with leaves on the flowering spike.
cards.keyFeatures: Pterostylis striata is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and when not flowering, a rosette of between five and nine dark green, wrinkled leaves, 4–15 mm (0.2–0.6 in) long and 3–9 mm (0.1–0.4 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Common Podolepis
cards.subtitle: Podolepis decipiens
cards.description: Podolepis decipiens, commonly known as deceiving copperwire-daisy, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and grows in Victoria, Tasmania and New South Wales. It is an upright, perennial herb with yellow daisy-like flowers on a single stem rising from a sparse rosette.
cards.keyFeatures: Podolepis decipiens is a perennial herb to 70 cm (28 in) high with a single upright or several woolly stems from a rootstock that is renewed yearly.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Tall Daisy
cards.subtitle: Brachyscome diversifolia
cards.description: Recorded 45 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) graeme lunt, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Broad-leaved Woodruff
cards.subtitle: Asperula euryphylla
cards.description: Recorded 45 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) J. Sayers, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Australian Hollyhock
cards.subtitle: Malva preissiana
cards.description: Malva preissiana, the Australian hollyhock or native hollyhock, is a herbaceous perennial in the family Malvaceae, found in all Australian states. It is a large herb, growing up to 3 metres high and up to 3 metres wide, depending on the number of stalks or branches, that the bush has. It is a short lived perennial living around 3–5 years.
cards.keyFeatures: The name Malva has its origins in the Greek word μαλακός ("malakos"), which can be roughly translated to mean "soft" and/or "smooth", and preissiana is derived from the name Joann August Ludwig Preiss, who was a well-known German botanist who spent up to four years in Australia studying native plants during the late 1800s.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Purple Fuzzweed
cards.subtitle: Vittadinia cuneata
cards.description: Vittadinia cuneata commonly known as fuzzy New Holland daisy,it is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is an upright perennial with variable leaves, blue or mauve flowers and grows in all mainland states of Australia and Tasmania.
cards.keyFeatures: Vittadinia cuneata is an upright annual or perennial, 10–40 cm (3.9–15.7 in) high, stiff stems and more or less covered in glandular, coarse, rough hairs. Leaves are variable in colour, sometimes green or grey-green, wedge-shaped, occasionally with lobes, 10–25 mm (0.39–0.98 in) long and 2–5 mm (0.079–0.197 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Max Campbell, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Max Campbell

cards.name: Swamp Mazus
cards.subtitle: Mazus pumilio
cards.description: Mazus pumilio, commonly known as the swamp mazus, is a plant native to eastern Australia, Tasmania and New Zealand. It is commonly cultivated as an ornamental plant, most often for creating a groundcover. It is a completely prostrate, perennial herb usually forming wide spreading patches.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Small Triggerplant
cards.subtitle: Stylidium despectum
cards.description: Recorded 41 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Thornhill, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Thornhill

cards.name: Slender Dock
cards.subtitle: Rumex brownii
cards.description: Rumex brownii, the hooked dock, Browne's dock or swamp dock, is a leafy perennial herb native to Australia, and is widespread and grows in disturbed sites. It is an introduced weed in the Pacific Islands, England, Japan, and New Zealand. It is 50–80 cm high with variably shaped basal leaves, oblong or lanceolate, to 12 cm long, and to 4 cm wide with cordate to truncate base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Martin Hannan-Jones, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Martin Hannan-Jones

cards.name: Blue Flax-lily
cards.subtitle: Dianella caerulea
cards.description: Dianella caerulea, commonly known as the blue flax-lily, blueberry lily, or paroo lily, is a perennial herb of the family Asphodelaceae, subfamily Hemerocallidoideae, found across the eastern states of Australia and Tasmania. It is a hardy plant, growing to a height and width of around 1 metre with grass-like strappy leaves. Blue flowers in spring and summer are followed by indigo-coloured berries.
cards.keyFeatures: Dianella caerulea is a strappy herbaceous fruit bearing plant to about 1 metre (3 ft) high, with a thick spreading rhizome under the ground. The bright green leaves have straight or toothed margins, and may reach 75 cm (30 in) in length and 0.3-2.5 cm wide.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Vale Jenny Conolly

cards.name: Pygmy Sundew
cards.subtitle: Drosera pygmaea
cards.description: Drosera pygmaea is a carnivorous, rosette-forming biennial or annual species of herb native to Australia and New Zealand. The specific epithet, which translates as "dwarf" from Latin, is a reference to the very small size of this plant, which grows to between 8 and 18 mm in diameter. Small, pale flowers are produced at the ends of 1- to 3-inch stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Sea Rimu
cards.subtitle: Caulerpa brownii
cards.description: Caulerpa brownii is a species of seaweed in the Caulerpaceae family. It was first described in 1843. It is native to Australia and New Zealand.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Rock Isotome
cards.subtitle: Lithotoma axillaris
cards.description: Isotoma axillaris, commonly known as rock isotome or showy isotome, is a small herbaceous perennial in the family Campanulaceae. It usually has blue or mauve star-shaped flowers from September to May. It may also be called blue star, star flower, or laurentia.
cards.keyFeatures: Isotoma axillaris is an upright perennial herb growing to 50 cm high with ascending stems that are often a purplish colour and covered with short, soft hairs quickly becoming smooth. The leaves are about 1.5–15 cm (0.59–5.91 in) long and 0.5–5 mm (0.020–0.197 in) wide with deep, toothed, linear lobes sharply pointed at the apex.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Common Cudweed
cards.subtitle: Euchiton involucratus
cards.description: Euchiton involucratus, the common cudweed, is an herb in the tribe Gnaphalieae within the family Asteraceae. It is native to Australia and New Zealand and sparingly naturalized in a few scattered locations in the United States (California + Massachusetts). Euchiton involucratus is a biennial or perennial herb up to 40 cm (16 inches) tall, spreading by means of stolons running along the surface of the ground.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by yatesy

cards.name: Rosella Spider-orchid
cards.subtitle: Caladenia rosella
cards.description: Caladenia rosella, commonly known as the rosella spider orchid, is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a ground orchid with a single hairy leaf and a single scented pink flower. Although it may have had a wider distribution in the past, the total number of plants in 2000 was estimated to be 120 in four populations in Victoria.
cards.keyFeatures: Caladenia rosella is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single erect, hairy leaf, 40–90 mm (2–4 in) long and 5–8 mm (0.2–0.3 in) wide. A single pale or bright pink flower 50–60 mm (2.0–2.4 in) wide is borne on a stalk 100–170 mm (4–7 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Australian Tumbleweed
cards.subtitle: Salsola australis
cards.description: Salsola australis, commonly known as the buckbush, rolypoly, soft rolypoly, or prickly saltwort, and has the Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara name Tjilkala is a species of flowering plant in the genus Salsola. And is found in all regions of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Salsola australis is a small annual spiky plant that grows tall or as a hemisphere from 60 to 100 cm (24 to 39 in) tall. Leaves are 10-30mm long begin cylindrical and bent downwards, becoming hastate with age.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Adam J. Searcy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Adam J. Searcy

cards.name: Fragrant Leek Orchid
cards.subtitle: Prasophyllum odoratum
cards.description: Prasophyllum odoratum, commonly known as fragrant leek orchid, Rogers scented leek orchid or sweet leek orchid is a species of orchid endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has a single tubular leaf and up to fifty fragrant green and white flowers with reddish marks.
cards.keyFeatures: Prasophyllum odoratum is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single tube-shaped leaf up to 700 mm (30 in) long and 2–8 mm (0.08–0.3 in) wide with a purplish base. Between ten and fifty flowers are arranged along a flowering spike 60–200 mm (2–8 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eamonn Culhane, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Scented Groundsel
cards.subtitle: Senecio odoratus
cards.description: Recorded 37 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Nataprawira, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Nataprawira

cards.name: Frosted Goosefoot
cards.subtitle: Chenopodium desertorum
cards.description: Chenopodium desertorum, common name frosted goosefruit, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, indigenous to Australia where it is found in all mainland states.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Mountain Apple-berry
cards.subtitle: Billardiera macrantha
cards.description: Billardiera macrantha is a species of flowering plant in the family Pittosporaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a slender twiner with narrowly elliptic leaves and yellowish-green flowers arranged singly on thin, pendent peduncles. This species is often confused with the similar Tasmanian endemic, Billardiera longiflora.
cards.keyFeatures: Billardiera macrantha is a slender twiner with shiny brown stems. Its adult leaves are narrowly elliptic, 24–53 mm (0.94–2.09 in) long and 4–8 mm (0.16–0.31 in) wide on a petiole 2–5 mm (0.079–0.197 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Matt Berger, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Matt Berger

cards.name: Buloke Mistletoe
cards.subtitle: Amyema linophylla
cards.description: Recorded 36 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) gmgoods, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by gmgoods

cards.name: Pimpernel Sundew
cards.subtitle: Drosera glanduligera
cards.description: Drosera glanduligera, commonly known as the pimpernel sundew or scarlet sundew, is a species of carnivorous plant in the Sundew family, Droseraceae. It is endemic to southern Australia. It is an ephemeral annual plant that grows in the winter and flowers from August to November.
cards.keyFeatures: Drosera glanduligera is a small herbaceous plant with 15 to 20 concave spathulate leaves, each only 8–20 mm (0.31–0.79 in) long, arranged in a convex to nearly flat rosette. When flowering it produces an erect glandular-hirsute stem up to 10 mm (0.39 in) tall bearing several orange flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) pimelea, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by pimelea

cards.name: Bonfire Liverwort
cards.subtitle: Marchantia berteroana
cards.description: Marchantia berteroana is a liverwort species in the genus Marchantia.
cards.keyFeatures: Marchantia berteroana is a flat, thalloid liverwort, with thallus up to 2 cm (0.79 in) long and 1.2 cm (0.47 in) wide. The thallus colour can range from dark green to yellow with a glossy surface, and is attached to the ground via rhizoids.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Steve Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Steve Kerr

cards.name: Fairy Fan-flower
cards.subtitle: Scaevola aemula
cards.description: Scaevola aemula, commonly known as the fairy fan-flower or common fan-flower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Goodeniaceae. It has mostly egg-shaped leaves and blue, mauve or white fan-shaped flowers. It grows in New South Wales, South Australia, Victoria and Western Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Scaevola aemula is a mat-forming, perennial herb that grows up to 50 cm high with brown, coarsely hairy, terete stems. The leaves are elliptic to egg-shaped tapering near the base, sessile, edges toothed, up to 10–88 mm (0.39–3.46 in) long and 4–31 mm (0.16–1.22 in) wide, decreasing in size near the flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nemracc, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Clover Glycine
cards.subtitle: Glycine latrobeana
cards.description: Glycine latrobeana, the clover glycine or Australian anchor plant, is a species of perennial herb endemic to south-eastern Australia. Its leaves are similar in appearance to the common pasture clover. It is native to Tasmania, Victoria, New South Wales and South Australia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Minnie Daisy
cards.subtitle: Minuria leptophylla
cards.description: Minuria leptophylla, commonly known as minnie daisy, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae endemic to mainland Australia. It is a perennial herb with white to pale lilac daisy-like flower heads and occurs throughout arid and semi-arid inland regions of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Minuria leptophylla is a perennial herb typically growing to 20–50 cm (7.9–19.7 in) high and branching near the base. The species commonly exhibits a decumbent to ascending growth habit, although erect forms occasionally occur.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Small River Buttercup
cards.subtitle: Ranunculus amphitrichus
cards.description: Ranunculus amphitrichus commonly known as the small river buttercup, is a flowering plant in the family Ranunculaceae. It has glossy green leaves, daisy-like yellow flowers and grows in Western Australia, southeastern Australia and New Zealand.
cards.keyFeatures: Ranunculus amphitrichus is an aquatic perennial, stems arising from leaf clusters and sparsely covered with soft, weak, thin hairs or smooth.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lek Khauv, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blue Fairy Orchid
cards.subtitle: Pheladenia deformis
cards.description: Pheladenia deformis, commonly known as blue fairy orchid or blue beard is the only species of the flowering plant genus Pheladenia in the orchid family, Orchidaceae and is endemic to Australia. It was originally named as Caladenia deformis and has since had several name changes. Plants have a single, narrow, hairy leaf and usually blue flowers with relatively short, broad sepals and petals and an unusual labellum.
cards.keyFeatures: Pheladenia deformis is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, sympodial herb with a few inconspicuous, fine roots and a tuber partly surrounded by a fibrous sheath. The tuber produces two "droppers" which become daughter tubers in the following year.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Hugo Innes, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Hugo Innes

cards.name: Pinnate-leaved Groundsel
cards.subtitle: Senecio pinnatifolius
cards.description: Senecio pinnatifolius is a species of herb native to Australia. Common names include coast groundsel, dune groundsel and variable groundsel.
cards.keyFeatures: It grows as an erect herb up to a metre in height, with yellow flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Dotted Duckweed
cards.subtitle: Landoltia punctata
cards.description: Spirodela punctata (or Landoltia punctata, common name dotted duckweed) is a species of duckweed (Lemnoideae). The species is morphologically intermediate between Lemna and other species of Spirodela. In 1999 D.H.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Joe Dillon, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Joe Dillon

cards.name: Fairy Aprons
cards.subtitle: Utricularia dichotoma
cards.description: Utricularia dichotoma, commonly known as fairy aprons, is a variable, perennial species of terrestrial bladderwort. It has mauve or purple fan-shaped flowers on a slender stalk and usually grows in wet locations. It is a widespread species in Australia and New Zealand, and was first described in 1805.
cards.keyFeatures: Utricularia dichotoma is a perennial herb with numerous underground trailing stems with bladders 1.5–2 mm (0.06–0.08 in) in diameter. It has absent or a few oval, spoon-shaped to narrow-lanceolate leaves 2–4 mm (0.08–0.16 in) long and up to 40 mm (1.6 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Large-spotted Sun Orchid
cards.subtitle: Thelymitra juncifolia
cards.description: Thelymitra juncifolia, known as large-spotted sun orchid, is a species of orchid that is endemic to south-eastern Australia and to New Zealand. It has a single thin, dark green leaf and up to five blue flowers with relatively large, dark blue spots on the dorsal sepal and petals. It is similar to T. ixioides but has fewer, smaller flowers with larger dark blue spots.
cards.keyFeatures: Thelymitra juncifolia is a tuberous, perennial herb with a single channelled, dark green thread-like to lance-shaped leaf 150–200 mm (6–8 in) long and 8–10 mm (0.3–0.4 in) wide. There are up to five greyish blue to light blue flowers with relatively large darker blue spots on the dorsal sepal and petals.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Prickly Woodruff
cards.subtitle: Asperula scoparia
cards.description: Asperula scoparia is a species of flowering plant in the family Rubiaceae. It was first described in 1847 and is endemic to Tasmania, Victoria and New South Wales in Australia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Pink Purslane
cards.subtitle: Parakeelya calyptrata
cards.description: Rumicastrum calyptratum (synonym Calandrinia calyptrata), the pink purslane or small-leaved parakeelya, is an annual plant in the family Montiaceae. It is endemic to Australia. The species occurs in Western Australia, South Australia, Victoria, Queensland, Tasmania, and New South Wales.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rosalie Lawrence, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rosalie Lawrence

cards.name: Common Sunray
cards.subtitle: Triptilodiscus pygmaeus
cards.description: Triptilodiscus is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gnaphalieae within the family Asteraceae. Species The only known species is Triptilodiscus pygmaeus, called the common sunray. It is native to Australia, found in all six states plus the Northern Territory.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Claudia Schipp

cards.name: Tiny Pennywort
cards.subtitle: Hydrocotyle callicarpa
cards.description: Recorded 30 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson
